sanskrit: agnihotraparispando dharmarātrisamāsanam somayajñābhyanujñānaṃ pañcamī yajñadakṣiṇā
english: Diligent tending of the sacred fire-offering, the keeping of the holy night-vigil, sanction for the soma-sacrifice, and the sacrificial fee as the fifth duty—

sanskrit: nityaṃ yajñakriyā dharmaḥ pitṛdevārcane ratiḥ sarvātithyaṃ ca kartavyam annenoñchārjitena vai
english: the constant performance of sacrifice is dharma, delight in the worship of the ancestors and the gods, and hospitality to all must be offered with food gathered by gleaning.

sanskrit: nivṛttir upabhogasya gorasānāṃ ca vai ratiḥ sthaṇḍile śayanaṃ yogaḥ śākaparṇaniṣevaṇam
english: Abstention from enjoyment of pleasures, contentment with the milk of the cow, sleeping upon the bare ground, the practice of yoga, and subsisting on herbs and leaves;

sanskrit: phalamūlāśanaṃ vāyur āpaḥ śaivalabhakṣaṇam ṛṣīṇāṃ niyamā hy ete yair jayanty ajitāṃ gatim
english: eating fruits and roots, living on air and water, and feeding on moss—these indeed are the observances of the sages, by which they win the goal that none else attains.

sanskrit: vidhūme nyastamusale vyaṅgāre bhuktavaj jane atītapātrasaṃcāre kāle vigatabhaikṣake
english: When the smoke has cleared, the pestle is laid aside, the embers are gone, the household has finished eating, the round of the serving-vessels is past, and the hour for begging is over—

sanskrit: atithiṃ kāṅkṣamāṇo vai śeṣānnakṛtabhojanaḥ satyadharmaratiḥ kṣānto munidharmeṇa yujyate
english: awaiting a guest, taking his meal of what food remains, delighting in truth and dharma, patient and serene—such a man is joined to the law of the sage.

sanskrit: na stambhī na ca mānī yo na pramatto na vismitaḥ mitrāmitrasamo maitro yaḥ sa dharmavid uttamaḥ
english: He who is neither stiff with pride nor vain, neither heedless nor bewildered, friendly and the same toward friend and foe alike—he is the highest knower of dharma.

sanskrit: umovāca deśeṣu ramaṇīyeṣu girīṇāṃ nirjhareṣu ca sravantīnāṃ ca kuñjeṣu parvatopavaneṣu ca
english: Umā said: In delightful regions, by the cascades of the mountains, in the bowers along the flowing streams, and in the groves upon the hills,

sanskrit: deśeṣu ca vicitreṣu phalavatsu samāhitāḥ mūlavatsu ca deśeṣu vasanti niyatavratāḥ
english: and in varied lands abounding in fruit and rich in roots, there dwell those of steadfast vows, their minds collected.

sanskrit: teṣām api vidhiṃ puṇyaṃ śrotum icchāmi śaṃkara vānaprastheṣu deveśa svaśarīropajīviṣu
english: I wish to hear, O Śaṃkara, the holy rule of these too—of the forest-dwellers, O lord of gods, who live by the labor of their own bodies.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca vānaprastheṣu yo dharmas taṃ me śṛṇu samāhitā śrutvā caikamanā devi dharmabuddhiparā bhava
english: Maheśvara said: Hear from me, with mind composed, the dharma that belongs to the forest-hermits; and having heard it single-mindedly, O goddess, let your thought be set wholly upon dharma.

sanskrit: saṃsiddhair niyataiḥ sadbhir vanavāsam upāgataiḥ vānaprasthair idaṃ karma kartavyaṃ śṛṇu yādṛśam
english: By the accomplished, the disciplined, the good who have taken up dwelling in the forest—by such forest-hermits this rite is to be performed; hear of what kind it is.

sanskrit: trikālam abhiṣekārthaḥ pitṛdevārcanaṃ kriyā agnihotraparispanda iṣṭihomavidhis tathā
english: Bathing thrice at the three times of day, the rite of worshipping ancestors and gods, diligent tending of the fire-offering, and the procedure of sacrifice and oblation;

sanskrit: nīvāragrahaṇaṃ caiva phalamūlaniṣevaṇam iṅgudair aṇḍatailānāṃ snehārthaṃ ca niṣevaṇam
english: the gathering of wild rice, the eating of fruits and roots, and the use of oils pressed from the seeds of the iṅgudī for their unctuous nourishment;

sanskrit: yogacaryākṛtaiḥ siddhaiḥ kāmakrodhavivarjanam vīraśayyām upāsadbhir vīrasthānopasevibhiḥ
english: by the perfected who follow the practice of yoga, the casting off of desire and anger; by those who keep the hero's couch and resort to the hero's posture;

sanskrit: yuktair yogavahaiḥ sadbhir grīṣme pañcatapais tathā maṇḍūkayoganiyatair yathānyāyaniṣevibhiḥ
english: by the steadfast yoked in yoga, the good, who in summer endure the five fires, who keep the frog-posture of yoga and observe each rule according to the ordinance;

sanskrit: vīrāsanagatair nityaṃ sthaṇḍile śayanais tathā śītayogo 'gniyogaś ca cartavyo dharmabuddhibhiḥ
english: by those ever seated in the hero's pose and sleeping upon the bare ground, the discipline of cold and the discipline of fire are to be practiced by minds bent upon dharma.

sanskrit: abbhakṣair vāyubhakṣaiś ca śaivālottarabhojanaiḥ aśmakuṭṭais tathā dāntaiḥ saṃprakṣālais tathāparaiḥ
english: By those who feed on water and on air, whose chief food is moss; by the self-restrained who pound their grain with stones, and by others who wash and cleanse their food;

sanskrit: cīravalkalasaṃvītair mṛgacarmanivāsibhiḥ kāryā yātrā yathākālaṃ yathādharmaṃ yathāvidhi
english: by those clad in bark-cloth and wearing the skins of deer—the round of life is to be carried out according to the season, according to dharma, according to the ordinance.

sanskrit: vananityair vanacarair vanapair vanagocaraiḥ vanaṃ gurum ivāsādya vastavyaṃ vanajīvibhiḥ
english: By those constant to the forest, who roam the forest, who guard it and range within it, the forest is to be approached as though it were a guru, and there the forest-dwellers must abide.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ homakriyā dharmaḥ pañcayajñaniṣevaṇam nāgapañcamayajñasya vedoktasyānupālanam
english: For them the rite of oblation is dharma, the observance of the five great sacrifices, and the keeping of the Veda-ordained sacrifice on the fifth day sacred to the serpents.

sanskrit: aṣṭamīyajñaparatā cāturmāsyaniṣevaṇam paurṇamāsyāṃ tu yo yajño nityayajñas tathaiva ca
english: Devotion to the sacrifice on the eighth day, the observance of the four-monthly rites, the sacrifice performed at the full moon, and likewise the perpetual sacrifice—

sanskrit: vimuktā dārasaṃyogair vimuktāḥ sarvasaṃkaraiḥ vimuktāḥ sarvapāpaiś ca caranti munayo vane
english: freed from union with wives, freed from all defilement, and freed from every sin, the sages wander in the forest.

sanskrit: srugbhāṇḍaparamā nityaṃ tretāgniśaraṇāḥ sadā santaḥ satpathanityā ye te yānti paramāṃ gatim
english: Holding the sacrificial ladle and vessels as their highest treasure, ever taking refuge in the three sacred fires, the good who keep always to the path of the good—they attain the supreme goal.

sanskrit: brahmalokaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ somalokaṃ ca śāśvatam gacchanti munayaḥ siddhā ṛṣidharmavyapāśrayāt
english: To the world of Brahmā, of great merit, and to the eternal world of Soma the perfected sages go, by their reliance upon the dharma of the seers.

sanskrit: eṣa dharmo mayā devi vānaprasthāśritaḥ śubhaḥ vistareṇārthasaṃpanno yathāsthūlam udāhṛtaḥ
english: This auspicious dharma resting upon the forest-hermits, O goddess, rich in meaning, I have set forth to you at length in its broad outline.

sanskrit: umovāca bhagavan devadeveśa sarvabhūtanamaskṛta yo dharmo munisaṃghasya siddhivādeṣu taṃ vada
english: Umā said: O blessed one, lord of the lords of gods, to whom all beings bow, tell me the dharma of the company of sages who dwell amid the teachings of perfection.

sanskrit: siddhivādeṣu saṃsiddhās tathā vananivāsinaḥ svairiṇo dārasaṃyuktās teṣāṃ dharmaḥ kathaṃ smṛtaḥ
english: Those perfected in the teachings of perfection and likewise dwelling in the forest, who live freely and yet keep the company of wives—how is their dharma declared?

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca svairiṇas tāpasā devi sarve dāravihāriṇaḥ teṣāṃ mauṇḍyaṃ kaṣāyaś ca vāsarātriś ca kāraṇam
english: Maheśvara said: Those ascetics who live freely, O goddess, all of whom take their pleasure with wives—for them the shaven head, the ochre robe, and the measured division of day and night are the means.

sanskrit: trikālam abhiṣekaś ca hotraṃ tv ṛṣikṛtaṃ mahat samādhiḥ satpathasthānaṃ yathoditaniṣevaṇam
english: Bathing at the three times of day, the great oblation performed as the seers ordained, deep meditation, standing fast upon the path of the good, and observance as has been declared;

sanskrit: ye ca te pūrvakathitā dharmā vananivāsinām yadi sevanti dharmāṃs tān āpnuvanti tapaḥphalam
english: and those duties of the forest-dwellers spoken of before—if they observe these duties, they obtain the fruit of austerity.

sanskrit: ye ca daṃpatidharmāṇaḥ svadāraniyatendriyāḥ caranti vidhidṛṣṭaṃ tad ṛtukālābhigāminaḥ
english: And those who keep the dharma of the married pair, their senses restrained to their own wives, who approach them only in the fertile season as the ordinance prescribes,

sanskrit: teṣām ṛṣikṛto dharmo dharmiṇām upapadyate na kāmakārāt kāmo 'nyaḥ saṃsevyo dharmadarśibhiḥ
english: for them, righteous as they are, the dharma laid down by the seers is fulfilled; for no other desire arising from mere lust is to be indulged by those who behold dharma.

sanskrit: sarvabhūteṣu yaḥ samyag dadāty abhayadakṣiṇām hiṃsāroṣavimuktātmā sa vai dharmeṇa yujyate
english: He who rightly grants to all beings the gift of fearlessness, his self freed from violence and anger—he indeed is joined with dharma.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtānukampī yaḥ sarvabhūtārjavavrataḥ sarvabhūtātmabhūtaś ca sa vai dharmeṇa yujyate
english: He who is compassionate toward all beings, vowed to uprightness toward all beings, and who has become one in spirit with all beings—he indeed is joined with dharma.

sanskrit: sarvavedeṣu vā snānaṃ sarvabhūteṣu cārjavam ubhe ete same syātām ārjavaṃ vā viśiṣyate
english: Bathing at all the sacred waters, and uprightness toward all beings—these two might be held equal, or else uprightness is the greater.

sanskrit: ārjavaṃ dharma ity āhur adharmo jihma ucyate ārjaveneha saṃyukto naro dharmeṇa yujyate
english: Uprightness, they say, is dharma; crookedness is called unrighteousness. A man here endowed with uprightness is joined with dharma.

sanskrit: ārjavo bhuvane nityaṃ vasaty amarasaṃnidhau tasmād ārjavanityaḥ syād ya icched dharmam ātmanaḥ
english: The upright man dwells forever in the world near the immortals; therefore let him be constant in uprightness who desires dharma for himself.

sanskrit: kṣānto dānto jitakrodho dharmabhūto 'vihiṃsakaḥ dharme ratamanā nityaṃ naro dharmeṇa yujyate
english: Patient, self-controlled, having conquered anger, become the very embodiment of dharma, doing no harm, his mind ever delighting in dharma—such a man is joined with dharma.

sanskrit: vyapetatandro dharmātmā śakyā satpatham āśritaḥ cāritraparamo buddho brahmabhūyāya kalpate
english: Free of sloth, righteous in soul, capable, holding to the path of the good, supreme in conduct and awakened, he becomes fit for union with Brahman.

sanskrit: umovāca āśramābhiratā deva tāpasā ye tapodhanāḥ dīptimantaḥ kayā caiva caryayātha bhavanti te
english: Umā said: O god, the ascetics who delight in the hermitage, those rich in austerity and radiant with splendor—by what observance do they become so?

sanskrit: rājāno rājaputrāś ca nirdhanā vā mahādhanāḥ karmaṇā kena bhagavan prāpnuvanti mahāphalam
english: Kings and the sons of kings, the poor or the greatly wealthy—by what deed, O blessed one, do they obtain the great fruit?

sanskrit: nityaṃ sthānam upāgamya divyacandanarūṣitāḥ kena vā karmaṇā deva bhavanti vanagocarāḥ
english: Having reached the eternal abode, anointed with celestial sandal—by what deed, O god, do they become rangers of the forest?

sanskrit: etaṃ me saṃśayaṃ deva tapaścaryāgataṃ śubham śaṃsa sarvam aśeṣeṇa tryakṣa tripuranāśana
english: Resolve for me this doubt of mine, O god, concerning the holy practice of austerity; declare it all without remainder, O three-eyed one, destroyer of the Three Cities.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca upavāsavratair dāntā ahiṃsrāḥ satyavādinaḥ saṃsiddhāḥ pretya gandharvaiḥ saha modanty anāmayāḥ
english: Maheśvara said: Tamed by vows of fasting, doing no harm, speaking the truth, and made perfect, after death they rejoice free of all ill in the company of the gandharvas.

sanskrit: maṇḍūkayogaśayano yathāsthānaṃ yathāvidhi dīkṣāṃ carati dharmātmā sa nāgaiḥ saha modate
english: He of righteous soul who, lying in the frog-posture of yoga, keeps his consecration according to place and ordinance, rejoices in the company of the serpent-nāgas.

sanskrit: śaṣpaṃ mṛgamukhotsṛṣṭaṃ yo mṛgaiḥ saha sevate dīkṣito vai mudā yuktaḥ sa gacchaty amarāvatīm
english: He who, consecrated and filled with joy, feeds among the deer on the grass cast off from their mouths, goes to Amarāvatī, the city of the immortals.

sanskrit: śaivālaṃ śīrṇaparṇaṃ vā tad vrato yo niṣevate śītayogavaho nityaṃ sa gacchet paramāṃ gatim
english: He who, bound to that vow, feeds on moss or on fallen leaves, ever bearing the discipline of cold, may attain the supreme goal.

sanskrit: vāyubhakṣo 'mbubhakṣo vā phalamūlāśano 'pi vā yakṣeṣv aiśvaryam ādhāya modate 'psarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ
english: He who lives on air or on water, or who eats fruits and roots, attains lordship among the yakṣas and rejoices amid the troops of apsarases.

sanskrit: agniyogavaho grīṣme vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā cīrtvā dvādaśa varṣāṇi rājā bhavati pārthivaḥ
english: He who in summer bears the discipline of fire, performing for twelve years the rite seen in the ordinance, becomes a king who rules the earth.

sanskrit: āhāraniyamaṃ kṛtvā munir dvādaśavārṣikam maruṃ saṃsādhya yatnena rājā bhavati pārthivaḥ
english: The sage who, observing restraint of food for twelve years and with effort mastering the desert wastes, becomes a king who rules the earth.

sanskrit: sthaṇḍile śuddham ākāśaṃ parigṛhya samantataḥ praviśya ca mudā yukto dīkṣāṃ dvādaśavārṣikīm
english: He who, upon the bare ground, taking the pure open sky as his shelter on every side, and entering with joy upon the twelve-year consecration—

sanskrit: sthaṇḍilasya phalāny āhur yānāni śayanāni ca gṛhāṇi ca mahārhāṇi candraśubhrāṇi bhāmini
english: the fruits of this couch on the bare ground, they say, O lovely one, are chariots and couches and houses of great worth, white as the moon.

sanskrit: ātmānam upajīvan yo niyato niyatāśanaḥ dehaṃ vānaśane tyaktvā sa svargaṃ samupāśnute
english: He who, living by his own self, restrained and restrained in food, casts off his body by fasting, attains to heaven.

sanskrit: ātmānam upajīvan yo dīkṣāṃ dvādaśavārṣikīm tyaktvā mahārṇave dehaṃ vāruṇaṃ lokam aśnute
english: He who, living by his own self through the twelve-year consecration, casts off his body in the great ocean, attains the world of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: ātmānam upajīvan yo dīkṣāṃ dvādaśavārṣikīm aśmanā caraṇau bhittvā guhyakeṣu sa modate
english: He who, living by his own self through the twelve-year consecration, breaks his feet upon a stone, rejoices among the guhyakas.

sanskrit: sādhayitvātmanātmānaṃ nirdvaṃdvo niṣparigrahaḥ cīrtvā dvādaśa varṣāṇi dīkṣām ekāṃ manogatām svargalokam avāpnoti devaiś ca saha modate
english: Having perfected the self by the self, beyond the pairs of opposites and free of possessions, having kept for twelve years the one consecration fixed in his mind, he attains the world of heaven and rejoices in the company of the gods.

sanskrit: ātmānam upajīvan yo dīkṣāṃ dvādaśavārṣikīm hutvāgnau deham utsṛjya vahniloke mahīyate
english: He who, living by his own self through the twelve-year consecration, offers himself in the fire and casts off his body, is exalted in the world of Agni.

sanskrit: yas tu devi yathānyāyaṃ dīkṣito niyato dvijaḥ ātmany ātmānam ādhāya nirdvaṃdvo niṣparigrahaḥ
english: But the twice-born who, O goddess, consecrated as the ordinance requires and restrained, having set the self within the self, beyond the pairs of opposites and free of possessions,

sanskrit: cīrtvā dvādaśa varṣāṇi dīkṣām ekāṃ manogatām araṇīsahitaṃ skandhe baddhvā gacchaty anāvṛtaḥ
english: having kept for twelve years the one consecration fixed in his mind, and bound the fire-sticks upon his shoulder, wanders forth uncovered—

sanskrit: vīrādhvānamanā nityaṃ vīrāsanaratas tathā vīrasthāyī ca satataṃ sa vīragatim āpnuyāt
english: his mind ever set on the hero's road, delighting in the hero's posture, and standing fast in the hero's place—he attains the goal of heroes.

sanskrit: sa śakralokago nityaṃ sarvakāmapuraskṛtaḥ divyapuṣpasamākīrṇo divyacandanabhūṣitaḥ sukhaṃ vasati dharmātmā divi devagaṇaiḥ saha
english: Gone forever to the world of Śakra, attended by every desire fulfilled, strewn with celestial flowers and adorned with celestial sandal, the righteous one dwells in bliss in heaven among the hosts of the gods.

sanskrit: vīralokagato vīro vīrayogavahaḥ sadā sattvasthaḥ sarvam utsṛjya dīkṣito niyataḥ śuciḥ vīrādhvānaṃ prapadyed yas tasya lokāḥ sanātanāḥ
english: The hero gone to the world of heroes, ever bearing the hero's discipline, steadfast in goodness, who renounces all and, consecrated, restrained, and pure, takes up the hero's road—for him the worlds are everlasting.

sanskrit: kāmagena vimānena sa vai carati cchandataḥ śakralokagataḥ śrīmān modate ca nirāmayaḥ
english: In a sky-chariot that goes where it wills he ranges at his pleasure, and gone to the world of Śakra, glorious and free of all ill, he rejoices.

sanskrit: umovāca bhagavan bhaganetraghna pūṣṇo daśanapātana dakṣakratuhara tryakṣa saṃśayo me mahān ayam
english: Umā said: O blessed one, slayer of Bhaga's eye, who struck out the teeth of Pūṣan, who ruined the sacrifice of Dakṣa, O three-eyed god, great is this doubt of mine.

sanskrit: cāturvarṇyaṃ bhagavatā pūrvaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ svayaṃbhuvā kena karmavipākena vaiśyo gacchati śūdratām
english: The four orders were of old created by the blessed Self-Existent One; by what ripening of deeds does a vaiśya pass into the state of a śūdra?

sanskrit: vaiśyo vā kṣatriyaḥ kena dvijo vā kṣatriyo bhavet pratilomaḥ kathaṃ deva śakyo dharmo niṣevitum
english: By what means does a vaiśya become a kṣatriya, or a twice-born become a kṣatriya? And how, O god, can dharma be observed against the natural order?

sanskrit: kena vā karmaṇā vipraḥ śūdrayonau prajāyate kṣatriyaḥ śūdratām eti kena vā karmaṇā vibho
english: By what deed is a brāhmaṇa born in the womb of a śūdra, and by what deed, O mighty one, does a kṣatriya pass into the state of a śūdra?

sanskrit: etaṃ me saṃśayaṃ deva vada bhūtapate 'nagha trayo varṇāḥ prakṛtyeha kathaṃ brāhmaṇyam āpnuyuḥ
english: Resolve for me this doubt, O god, lord of beings, sinless one: how may the three orders by their very nature attain to brāhmaṇa-hood?

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca brāhmaṇyaṃ devi duṣprāpaṃ nisargād brāhmaṇaḥ śubhe kṣatriyo vaiśyaśūdrau vā nisargād iti me matiḥ
english: Maheśvara said: Brāhmaṇa-hood, O goddess, is hard to win. By his very nature, O fair one, a brāhmaṇa is a brāhmaṇa; so too the kṣatriya, the vaiśya, and the śūdra are such by nature—this is my judgment.

sanskrit: karmaṇā duṣkṛteneha sthānād bhraśyati vai dvijaḥ jyeṣṭhaṃ varṇam anuprāpya tasmād rakṣeta vai dvijaḥ
english: By an evil deed here the twice-born falls from his station; therefore, having attained the highest order, let the twice-born guard it well.

sanskrit: sthito brāhmaṇadharmeṇa brāhmaṇyam upajīvati kṣatriyo vātha vaiśyo vā brahmabhūyāya gacchati
english: Whether a kṣatriya or a vaiśya, he who stands firm in the brāhmaṇa's dharma and lives by brāhmaṇa-hood goes toward union with Brahman.

sanskrit: yas tu vipratvam utsṛjya kṣātraṃ dharmaṃ niṣevate brāhmaṇyāt sa paribhraṣṭaḥ kṣatrayonau prajāyate
english: But he who, abandoning his brāhmaṇa-state, practices the dharma of the warrior, falls from brāhmaṇa-hood and is born in the womb of a kṣatriya.

sanskrit: vaiśyakarma ca yo vipro lobhamohavyapāśrayaḥ brāhmaṇyaṃ durlabhaṃ prāpya karoty alpamatiḥ sadā
english: And the brāhmaṇa of little understanding who, given over to greed and delusion, having attained brāhmaṇa-hood so hard to win, ever does the work of a vaiśya—

sanskrit: sa dvijo vaiśyatām eti vaiśyo vā śūdratām iyāt svadharmāt pracyuto vipras tataḥ śūdratvam āpnute
english: that twice-born passes into the state of a vaiśya, and a vaiśya likewise into the state of a śūdra; the brāhmaṇa fallen from his own dharma thereby attains the state of a śūdra.

sanskrit: tatrāsau nirayaṃ prāpto varṇabhraṣṭo bahiṣkṛtaḥ brahmalokaparibhraṣṭaḥ śūdraḥ samupajāyate
english: Then, fallen from his order and cast out, he comes to hell; fallen from the world of Brahman, he is born again as a śūdra.

sanskrit: kṣatriyo vā mahābhāge vaiśyo vā dharmacāriṇi svāni karmāṇy apāhāya śūdrakarmāṇi sevate
english: And the kṣatriya, O greatly blessed one, or the vaiśya, O practiser of dharma, who casts aside his own duties and follows the works of a śūdra—

sanskrit: svasthānāt sa paribhraṣṭo varṇasaṃkaratāṃ gataḥ brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdratvaṃ yāti tādṛśaḥ
english: fallen from his own station, he sinks into the confusion of the orders; such a brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, or vaiśya passes into the state of a śūdra.

sanskrit: yas tu śuddhaḥ svadharmeṇa jñānavijñānavāñ śuciḥ dharmajño dharmanirataḥ sa dharmaphalam aśnute
english: But he who is purified by his own dharma, possessed of knowledge and discernment, pure, knowing dharma and devoted to it—he enjoys the fruit of dharma.

sanskrit: idaṃ caivāparaṃ devi brahmaṇā samudīritam adhyātmaṃ naiṣṭhikaṃ sadbhir dharmakāmair niṣevyate
english: And there is this further teaching, O goddess, proclaimed by Brahmā: the highest spiritual doctrine, observed by the good who long for dharma.
